## Analyst notes (hypotheses and conclusions)
- **Training set is easy; scored pool is hard** (2026-10-15T21:56:38Z): GBFS(total length)+shortening solves 424/424 training problems; 422 shorter than the published certificates (7599 vs 14257 total moves). Known training paths never exceed the initial total length by more than 2 letters. On 200 random scored problems GBFS (5M nodes) solves only 44 (22%); solve rate is flat in initial length (15-40), so difficulty is structural.
- **Heuristic: cyclic length is worse** (2026-10-15T21:56:38Z): On 80 scored problems at 3M nodes: score=len 12/80; score=0.1len+cyc 0/80; 0.5len+0.5cyc 7/80. Cyclically-reduced length makes conjugate stacks x^k r x^-k a free plateau. Keep plain total length as GBFS key. Budget scaling: 15M nodes -> 19/80.
- **Pool is Miller-Schupp family; problems are AC-neighbours** (2026-10-15T21:56:38Z): 2937 problems contain (up to rotation/inversion) the MS relator x^-1 y^n x y^-(n+1) with n=1..10; the rest look AC-transformed. 44 solved paths' states lie within 2 moves of 10 other unsolved problems (one exactly on a path). Built corridor table: other problems' solution states act as terminals.
